:::{#exm-lempel-ziv-parsing}
#### The Lempel--Ziv code of a short message

<!-- no-figure: the example is a table of phrases and their pairs -->

The code below follows @def-lempel-ziv-parsing and @def-lempel-ziv-code
for the message $\text{aabababbabbbab}$.
It prints each phrase with its pair,
then the number of phrases
and the length in [bits](entropy.qmd#def-bit) of the code.

```{r}
#| label: lempel-ziv-code
message_text <- "aabababbabbbab"
symbols <- strsplit(message_text, "")[[1]]
phrases <- character(0)
current <- ""
for (symbol in symbols) {
  candidate <- paste0(current, symbol)
  if (candidate %in% phrases) {
    current <- candidate
  } else {
    phrases <- c(phrases, candidate)
    current <- ""
  }
}
phrase_length <- nchar(phrases)
prefixes <- substr(phrases, 1, phrase_length - 1)
positions <- match(prefixes, c("", phrases)) - 1
new_symbols <- substr(phrases, phrase_length, phrase_length)
data.frame(phrase = phrases, position = positions, symbol = new_symbols)
n_phrases <- length(phrases)
position_bits <- ceiling(log2(n_phrases))
code_bits <- n_phrases * (position_bits + 1)
c(phrases = n_phrases, code_bits = code_bits, leftover = nchar(current))
```

The message has $`r nchar(message_text)`$ symbols
and the parsing has $`r n_phrases`$ phrases,
so each position takes $`r position_bits`$ bits.
With one more bit for each new symbol,
the code has $`r code_bits`$ bits,
which is more than the $`r nchar(message_text)`$ bits of the message written as plain 0 and 1 symbols.
A message this short is too short for the code to save anything.

:::
